title: Kiosk Dashboard Timing and Filters
lede: The idle dashboard now tells staff how close a checkout is to its deadline and makes the count tiles' filter behavior visible before anyone has to guess or tap around.

stats.n: Near deadlines, today/tomorrow, weekday, and overdue age each get distinct copy
The tile row now explains that counts change the list below

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.note: Same iPad Air 11-inch simulator, same live kiosk fixture, same dashboard state. The clock/freshness stamp naturally advanced between captures; the row subtitle fix from the preceding slice is present in both captures.

pairs.title: Deadline and filter signals
pairs.sub: Look first at the due pills, then at the space immediately above the three metric tiles.
pairs.beforeCap: Every due pill used the same calendar-style timestamp, and the metric row relied on a small filter glyph with no visible instruction.
pairs.afterCap: The first row reads `Due today · 12:00 PM`, later rows use a concise weekday/time form, and the count row now says `Tap a count to filter the list`. Near-deadline and overdue variants are covered by source contracts.

changes.was: Absolute date text made a checkout due later today look like an ordinary future date and did not tell staff how close an overdue item was to its deadline.
changes.now: Dashboard-only copy uses `Due now`, `Due in …`, `Due today`, `Due tomorrow`, short weekday/date forms, and `Overdue · …`. Full timestamps remain on detail and edit surfaces.

changes.h: The metric row now explains its interaction
changes.was: The tiles looked like read-only KPI cards, with the filter affordance carried mostly by a small icon.
changes.now: A visible instruction sits above the tiles and the filter icon has stronger weight; the existing button states and accessibility hints remain intact.

verification: 18 focused Vitest source-contract tests pass across the idle dashboard, sleep-mode removal, and iOS quality contracts.
WisconsinKiosk Xcode build and run succeeds on the iPad Air 11-inch (M4) simulator, iOS 26.5.
Runtime snapshot exposes `Due today · 12:00 PM`, `Due Mon · 12:00 PM`, and the holder/count row context on active checkouts.
notes: The simulator fixture currently shows a due-today and future-day state. The `Due in …` and `Overdue · …` branches are source-tested and build-verified, but still deserve a live fixture/device replay during kiosk QA.
No API, schema, custody, or detail-surface behavior changed in this slice.
